anodised-black.purpose: The unlit bench: page ground, and the inside of an image well before its render loads.

machined-slate.purpose: Every raised surface — tiles, dialogs, inputs, the standing button. One step up from the ground, never two.

scribe-line.purpose: Hairline borders and dividers on chrome only. A scribed mark, not a drawn box.

chalk.purpose: Primary text, reserved for what the user is reading right now.

graphite.purpose: Secondary text, which is most text. Labels, metadata, resting controls.

layout-blue.purpose: The machinist's marking dye. Live interaction only — dragging, focus, selection. Never at rest.

display.purpose: The horizon. Library name, empty-state headline. At most one per viewport.

headline.purpose: A part's own name on its detail page.

title.purpose: Tile captions, dialog titles, the name of a thing in a list.

body.purpose: Prose, helper text, refusals. Capped at 70ch.

label.purpose: Section headings and metadata keys, uppercase and tracked.

mono.purpose: Machine identity: paths, hashes, part numbers. Selectable and exact.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers and menus only, always over a scrim. The only shadow in the system; a tile or button carrying one is a defect.

motion.name: ease-mechanical
motion.purpose: The only easing. Decisive out, settled in.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: State changes on controls: hover lift, label colour, metadata reveal.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: The global default on every transition; tile lift and larger surface changes.

motion.name: transition-property
motion.purpose: The only animatable properties. `translate` is named separately because Tailwind 4 compiles lift utilities to the independent property, and a list naming only `transform` animates nothing.

components.name: Mono Value
components.description: A pasteable machine string: selectable, exact, never middle-elided.

narrative.overview: A machinist's bench under a single task lamp. The parts are lit; the bench is not. Every surface exists to be the unlit surround for a rendered object — the ground is near-black, the chrome is grey on grey, and the only saturated colour appears when you are doing something. The register is quiet, precise and unhurried: trust is earned by being exact rather than emphatic, which is why secondary text outnumbers primary roughly fourteen to one. The one place the system permits weight is the display line, because a wall of identical tiles needs a horizon.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground; the render is the only lit thing on the page
Two type voices only — a heavy display horizon and a quiet body
One saturated colour, reserved for live interaction
Flat by tonal layering; no shadow except beneath an overlay
Image tiles borderless and edge-to-edge; chrome tiles hairlined
Motion is mechanical: transform and opacity, 120/180 ms, always reduced-motion aware

rules.name: The Marking Dye Rule
rules.body: Layout Blue appears only where something is happening — dragging, focused, selected, loading. If a screenshot taken at rest contains any Layout Blue, that is a defect. Its rarity is what makes it readable without a legend.

rules.name: The Two-Greys Rule
rules.body: Text is Chalk or Graphite and nothing between. A third text grey is how a hierarchy becomes a gradient nobody can parse.

rules.name: The One Step Up Rule
rules.body: A surface may sit exactly one tonal step above its parent. Two stacked panels get a scribe line between them, not two lightnesses.

rules.name: The Copyable Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a user might paste into another program is set in mono and is selectable, never elided with an ellipsis in the middle.

rules.name: The Self-Hosted Font Rule
rules.body: Lapidary ships into air-gapped deployments. Inter is self-hosted from the bundle, subset to Latin + Latin Extended-A so Turkish renders without a second file.

rules.name: The One Horizon Rule
rules.body: Exactly one Display line per viewport. A second is not a hierarchy, it is a competition.

rules.name: The Unlit Bench Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not cast shadows, because the light is on the parts, not on the furniture. The only shadow is the one an overlay throws by being in front of the page rather than in it.

rules.name: The Frameless Picture Rule
rules.body: Never put a border on a tile whose content is an image. The image is the edge.

dos: Do keep Layout Blue (#6ea8fe) for live interaction only. A resting screenshot containing it is a defect.
Do set every pasteable string — path, hash, part number — in mono, selectable, never middle-elided.
Do give every part tile its metadata on hover and on :focus-visible, so the keyboard reaches everything the mouse does.
Do ship one Display line per viewport and let it be genuinely heavy (900, -0.02em).
Do label every mesh-derived measurement as approximate wherever it appears, including inside dialogs and tooltips.
Do self-host Inter, subset to Latin + Latin Extended-A, so Turkish and an air-gapped install both work.
Do route every user-facing string through web/src/lib/strings.ts.
donts: Don't put a border on an image tile. The image is its own edge.
Don't add a box-shadow to anything that is not an overlay above a scrim.
Don't introduce a third text grey, a second accent hue, or a fourth radius.
Don't use a font weight between 500 and 900 — the gap between the body voice and the display voice is the hierarchy.
Don't let colour alone carry a state. Every state has a second cue.
Don't word an eviction so it reads as deletion, or a removal so it reads as a saving.
Don't animate anything but transform, translate and opacity, and never past 180ms for a state change.
